title: GSNA service record
description: One normalized government service. Corrects two flaws in the explain.md section-3 schema: (1) scam_warnings is REMOVED - scam data lives only in agents/scam_patterns.json so a scraper cannot write into it; (2) fees are a keyed lookup read directly by the composer, never retrieved by embedding similarity.

category.description: MUST be an id from data/taxonomy.json. Join key for retrieval filter and scam lookup.

office.description: Responsible office/ministry as printed by the source.

locality.description: Set when the service differs by place (trade_license, land_tax). null = nationally uniform. A locality-varying service with locality:null is a bug.

variants.description: Sub-cases within one service, e.g. passport new vs renewal, or 48-page vs 64-page. Keeps the taxonomy small without collapsing real differences.

source_url.description: Where THIS document requirement was read. Per-item, because doc lists are often assembled from several pages.

where.description: Online portal, or which office counter.

fees.description: KEYED LOOKUP, not free text. The composer reads this directly by fee_key; it is never embedded or vector-retrieved, because retrieving a fee by semantic similarity is the easiest way to state a wrong number.

amount_bdt.description: null means NOT VERIFIED. The composer must render 'not verified - check with the office', never guess or omit silently.

source_document.description: PDF circular/gazette this came from, if Tier 2.

source_last_updated.description: Self-declared update date of the page this fee came from. Per-fee because the document list and the fee schedule are different pages that go stale at different rates (observed: passport docs 2026-05-11, passport fees 2020-01-20).

raw_text.description: Verbatim fee cell from the source charter. Kept whenever parsing was refused (conditional/ratio/instalment pricing) so a human can read exactly what the government published instead of re-fetching.

contact.description: Phone/helpline, for services where the honest answer is 'call them'.

apply_portal.description: Transactional URL for the user. Usually a JS SPA we do NOT scrape.

source_url.description: Primary page this record was built from.

last_scraped_date.description: Date WE fetched the page. Says nothing about content age - see source_last_updated.

source_last_updated.description: The date the SOURCE PAGE declares its own content was last updated (extracted by tools/staleness.py). NOT the fetch date. Added after finding the passport fee page self-reports 2020-01-20 while last_scraped_date would read 2026-09-04 - scraping a stale page must not make it look fresh. The Freshness Agent MUST key on this field, falling back to last_scraped_date only when it is null (and then saying so).

verification.description: Required everywhere a factual claim is made. explain.md 5.1: an unverified fee can cost a real user money, so unverified must be representable and must render as such.

status.description: unverified = do not show as fact. source_read = read off an official page. human_confirmed = a person checked it against the source document or the office.

method.description: e.g. 'read PDF circular', 'phoned office', 'cross-checked news report'.
